title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook - Process, Runbooks, Rotations, and Templates
author: Priya Raman
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response process, standard runbook templates, postmortem requirements, rotation policies, game-day procedures, and customer/status-page communications templates. The goal is to ensure consistent, rapid response across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments while preserving a clear audit trail and continuous improvement loop.

Scope:
- Applies to all services supporting customer-facing inference (API gateway, runtime, autoscaler, model catalog, telemetry ingestion, dedicated pools, private control plane).
- Includes escalation paths to SRE, runtime, product, and security teams.
- Excludes local developer experiments and non-prod sandbox outages unless they affect production behaviour.

Incident severity definitions (triage):
1) Sev 1 (P0): Platform-wide outage or severe degradation affecting >20% of customers or critical SLAs (complete API failure, control plane unavailable). Response: immediate page, full incident bridge, executive comms.
2) Sev 2 (P1): Significant degradation to a subset of customers or features (high error rates, severe latency increase). Response: page on-call, assemble core responders, escalate as required.
3) Sev 3 (P2): Functional impact on non-critical features or single-customer impact without immediate SLA breach. Response: owner-driven response, triage, schedule fix.
4) Sev 4 (P3): Low-impact issues, informational, backlog items. Response: tracked in ticket queue; no immediate page.

Service level objectives (for triage reference):
- API request success rate: 99.9% monthly (alert threshold: 99.5% over 5m).
- P95 latency: 220ms (alert threshold: P95 > 350ms for 10m).
- Model inference queue length: alert if queued jobs > 3x normal for 15m.

Pager rules and alerting thresholds (examples):
- High error rate: >5% 5xx rate for API for 5m -> SEV2 page.
- Complete dataplane disconnect: control-plane cannot reach GPU fleet for 2m -> SEV1 page.
- SLO breach imminent: Error budget burn rate >10x for 30m -> SEV2 page.

On-call rotations and responsibilities:
- Teams with on-call: eng-sre (platform), eng-serving-runtime (runtime), eng-infra (cloud & networking), eng-private-deployments (customer on-prem escalations).
- Rotation cadence: 1-week primary rotation (Mon 09:00 UTC to next Mon 09:00 UTC). Secondary/backup rotations use 2-week stagger.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in PagerDuty notes):
  1. Summary of active incidents and severity.
  2. Runbooks in progress and current play stage.
  3. Known degradations or maintenance windows.
  4. Contacts reached and outstanding action items.
- On-call responsibilities:
  - Acknowledge pages within 5m for SEV1/SEV2.
  - Triage and contain within 30m for SEV1; within 60m for SEV2.
  - Escalate to team lead/secondary if unable to make progress in 15m (SEV1) or 30m (SEV2).
  - Document timeline and actions in the incident ticket (Jira) and in the incident bridge notes.

Incident response runbook template (use for all services):
- Title: short, descriptive.
- Impact: who/what is affected.
- Detection: monitoring/alert that triggered this runbook (metrics/logs).
- Quick checks (order matters):
  1. Check global status page and recent deploys.
  2. Verify control-plane connectivity: `curl -f https://controlplane.internal/health` (expect 200).
  3. Confirm GPU node health: `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide` and check node/taints.
  4. Review recent rollout/infra changes (CI/CD) in the last 30m.
- Containment steps:
  1. Route traffic to fallback model / region using routing-policy CLI: `ri routing deploy --fallback-model small-v1 --region us-west-2` (example).
  2. Increase autoscaler target if backlog is growing: update HPA/scale-set to +20% capacity.
  3. Disable recent canary if rollout suspected (by tag or deployment id).
- Remediation steps:
  1. Identify root cause logs: `rg "ERROR|panic|OOM" /var/log/runtime/*.log` and correlate with trace id.
  2. Apply hotfix (patch release or config rollback).
  3. Validate fix on staging then progressively ramp traffic (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Post-incident cleanup:
  - Re-enable normal autoscaling and routing policies.
  - Revoke temporary credentials and rollback emergency configs.
  - Open postmortem and assign owner within 24 hours.

Example runbook: High inference latency (queue backlog)
- Detection: P95 latency > 350ms for 10m AND inference queue length > baseline * 3.
- Quick checks:
  - Verify model shards and KV cache hits: `ri metrics query --name kv-cache-hit-rate --last 15m`
  - Check GPU utilization: `nvidia-smi` on representative nodes or `promql: avg(gpu_utilization)`
- Containment:
  - Temporarily enable prefix caching for common prompt paths: `ri cache enable --prefix /v1/generate/common`
  - Scale dedicated pool: `ri pool scale --pool-id pool-dedicated-42 --delta +2`
- Remediation:
  - Restart problematic worker pods with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-worker -n runtime`.
  - If OOM observed, apply quantization profile or reduce batch size.

Postmortem template (required for SEV1/SEV2):
- Title (one-line).
- Incident ID (Jira ticket).
- Severity, Date/time (start, mitigation, resolution).
- Summary (3-5 sentence customer-facing summary).
- Impact (customers affected, SLOs breached, estimated lost units).
- Root cause (concise).
- Timeline (ordered bullets with timestamps and actors).
- Contributing factors (technical, process, organizational).
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and due dates.
- Rollback or post-incident verification plan.
- Lessons learned and follow-ups (link to follow-up tickets).
- Reviewed by (names) and verification of closure.

Game-day (simulated incident) playbook:
- Frequency: quarterly cross-team game-days; platform-level once per quarter, team-specific twice a year.
- Objectives: validate paging, runbooks, SLO-based alerting, cross-team escalation, runbook accuracy, and postmortem process.
- Pre-game checklist:
  - Confirm participants and roles (facilitator, observers, primary on-call).
  - Freeze non-essential deploys during exercise window.
  - Prepare synthetic traffic generator and failure injection scripts.
- Running the game-day:
  1. Trigger simulated alert (metrics or synthetic).
  2. Allow on-call to triage and follow runbook steps.
  3. Observers score response on timeliness, communication, and runbook completeness.
  4. Run retro and capture action items as Jira tasks within 48 hours.

Status page and customer communications templates (use these for external updates):
- Status page component naming: `API (control-plane)`, `API (inference-dataplane)`, `Dedicated pools`, `Private control plane`.
- Status page update cadence: initial update within 30 minutes for SEV1, status cadence every 60 minutes until mitigation; for SEV2 initial update within 60 minutes and every 2 hours thereafter.

Status update template (public):
- Title: [Major outage] API (inference-dataplane) degraded \u2014 partial mitigation in progress
- Time: 2026-02-10T14:12Z
- Summary: We are seeing increased latency for inference requests in us-west-2. A subset of customers may experience timeouts and higher latencies. Engineering is investigating.
- Impact: Affected customers may see 5-30% increased latency; some requests may timeout.
- Current status: Engineering has identified a model caching regression and is applying a mitigation to fallback routing.
- Next update: 2026-02-10T15:12Z
- Contact: status@redwood-inference.internal

Customer email template (for SEV1):
- Subject: Incident report \u2014 API impact (start: 2026-02-10T14:05Z)
- Body:
  Hello,

  We are investigating an incident that began at 2026-02-10T14:05Z affecting the Redwood Inference API in us-west-2. Some customers may see increased latency or request timeouts. Our engineering team has applied a mitigation and we are working on a full resolution.

  Impact: Increased latency and intermittent timeouts for inference requests.
  Mitigation: Traffic temporarily routed to fallback model variants and additional capacity added to dedicated pools.
  Next update: within 60 minutes.

  We apologize for the disruption. If you have specific concerns please reply to this message or contact your account team.

  \u2014 Redwood Inference Support

Internal incident communication template (Slack/bridge):
- Channel: #incidents (public summary), #incidents-private (sensitive details)
- Initial post:
  SEV1: API inference-dataplane degraded (us-west-2). Impact: increased latency/timeouts. Primary on-call: @oncall-runtime (Priya). Bridge: link-to-bridge. Current action: fallback routing in progress.

Post-incident cadence and SLAs for documentation:
- Postmortem must be created and linked to the incident Jira within 24 hours of mitigation.
- Postmortem review with broader stakeholders (SRE, Runtime, Product, Sales/CS if customer-facing) within 5 business days.
- All long-term corrective actions must be tracked with owners and target dates; overdue items reviewed monthly by SRE leadership.

Operational tooling and artifacts (links & Examples):
- Incident ticket template (Jira project: INF-INC).
- PagerDuty schedule: `oncall-runtime-weekly`, `oncall-platform-weekly`.
- Runbooks stored in Confluence under `/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks`.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- On-call -> Team lead (10-15m) -> SRE manager -> Eng exec (for SEV1).
- Customer escalations -> CS -> Assigned SEV lead -> Eng exec if SLA impact.

Ownership and maintenance:
- This playbook is owned by eng-sre.
- Runbooks should be validated and updated after every game-day and major incident.
- Every service owner must review and confirm runbook accuracy quarterly.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and common checks
- Check API gateway errors (PromQL): `sum(rate(api_gateway_errors_total[5m])) by (code)`
- Check pod restarts: `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}\n'`
- Rollback last deploy: `ci rollback --service runtime-worker --to-revision <previous>`

Revision history:
- 2025-09-15: Initial draft (Priya Raman)
